text:
Amanda (CS): Heads up — AcmeCorp onboarding ramped faster than expected. Our spend forecast for their QBR jumped ~40% vs last week. Can we triage fast?
Ryan (FinOps): On it. Pulling projected burn now. Do we know which route/model is spiking (chat vs embeddings)?
Amanda (CS): Mostly embeddings and long-chat sessions from their pilot. They enabled bulk import of transcripts yesterday.
Meena (Success): Did they switch to the high-quality model by accident? I asked product but no answer yet.
Devon (Onboarding): We rolled a batch import job that splits into many parallel requests — that likely drove the burst. I can pause the job.
Ryan (FinOps): Pause ASAP pls. Also temporary mitigations: 1) throttle concurrency on the import job, 2) switch embeddings call to smaller model variant, 3) enable prefix caching for repeated docs. Which is fastest?
Devon (Onboarding): Pausing is 1-click. Throttle is trivial (we can add a token bucket in the batch runner). Switching model needs a config flip but doable now.
Amanda (CS): I'll tell the customer we're pausing the import and doing a short cost play to avoid QBR shock. Need a one-slide summary for QBR: impact, mitigations, ask (credits/commit). Can someone draft?
Ryan (FinOps): Drafting slide now. Quick numbers: projected additional monthly spend if unchecked = ~$12k; with throttling + model switch we reduce by ~65%.
Meena (Success): I'll capture the enablement ask: show them how to use smaller embedding model + dedupe uploads + use chunk-level caching. Also request they schedule a 30m ops walkthrough before QBR.
BudgetBot: :warning: Alert: AcmeCorp project ACME-42 exceeded 75% of monthly credits (current usage 78%).
Amanda (CS): Thanks bot. Ryan — can you add a recommended temporary quota we can push via the console?
Ryan (FinOps): Recommend soft cap at 60% of current rate and hard limit at 85% of monthly credits. I'll put exact numbers in the slide.
Devon (Onboarding): Paused the import job at 11:24am PT. Requeued smaller batches at reduced concurrency.
Amanda (CS): Nice. Meena — for the QBR deck can you include a short playbook: what we did, what we recommend (throttle, model switch, caching), and CTA for commit/credits or dedicated pool?
Meena (Success): Yep — will add 1 slide + an appendix with the bullet checklist for post-QBR ops.
Ryan (FinOps): Quick runbook snippet for engineers (put in Ops channel):
```
# throttle example (pseudo)
batch_runner.set_concurrency(8)
batch_runner.set_rate_limit(100/second)
# switch embeddings model
config.embedding_model = "embed-small-v1"
```
Amanda (CS): Perfect. Also capture renewal risk note: they see unexpected spend as a pain point. Our ask should emphasize quick wins + offer a 1-month credits buffer if needed to keep renewal healthy.
Meena (Success): Agreed. I'll propose a conditional credits buffer and a technical enablement session as part of the QBR.
BudgetBot: :white_check_mark: Action logged: incident-ACME-cost-surge created and assigned to #customer-success.
Amanda (CS): Action items: Ryan finalize slide (ETA 30m), Meena add playbook & credits ask, Devon confirm no further imports until we sign off, Amanda will coordinate customer message.
Devon (Onboarding): Confirmed — no new imports until we clear changes.
Ryan (FinOps): Slide shared in thread (link: https://redwood.internal/slides/acme-qbr-cost-1719008642). ETA done in 25m.
Amanda (CS): Thanks team. Meena — can you run the short enablement session before Thursday? QBR scheduled Friday.
Meena (Success): Yes — booking 30m slot tomorrow 10am PT and sending invite.
Amanda (CS): Closing loop here. We'll present mitigations in QBR and propose credits + optional Dedicated pool for predictable throughput. Will update thread after the enablement run. :thumbsup:
